body:
[aida:reviewer] #2030's MISSING CI IS DIAGNOSED. The PR CONFLICTS with main, and a commit
pushed to a conflicting PR produces no workflow run at all — not a failure, not a pending,
nothing. My F3 said "I do not know why and I am not guessing"; this is the answer, with
evidence.

THE EVIDENCE, in the order it settled:

    gh pr view 2030      mergeable=false   mergeable_state=dirty
    refs/pull/2030/head  05969aa3978d      (the new commit, pushed 04:52Z)
    refs/pull/2030/merge 8bcf8e9b565f      dated 2026-09-20 13:38:23 -0700
                         parents: a8c1877576 + 8ba48f5b98   <- the PREVIOUS head

    git merge-base --is-ancestor 05969aa397 8bcf8e9b56  ->  NO

I MUST CORRECT MY OWN FIRST HYPOTHESIS, which was that the merge ref would be absent. It
is not absent — it EXISTS and is STALE. It was computed at 13:38 for head 8ba48f5b98,
eight hours before the current commit landed, and the current head is not an ancestor of
it. GitHub could not recompute it against the conflict, so the pull_request event never
produced a runnable merge ref and no workflow was dispatched. Checking the ref's PARENTS
rather than its existence is what distinguished those two stories, and the existence check
alone would have sent me to the wrong conclusion.

I THEN CHECKED THE POPULATION, because "conflicting means no CI" was too clean to trust.
All 17 open PRs by mergeable_state and check-run count:

    blocked     14 PRs    checks 2-13     (the normal held state)
    dirty        3 PRs    #2030 checks=0, #1981 checks=3, #1989 checks=3
    unstable     1 PR     #2042 checks=17

SO CONFLICTING DOES NOT ALWAYS MEAN ZERO, and the difference is the ORDER OF EVENTS:

  main moved under a PR that already ran     -> head keeps its checks, they are just
                                                against a stale merge base (#1981, #1989)
  a commit is pushed while the PR conflicts  -> that commit never gets a run at all (#2030)

#2030 is the second case and it is the dangerous one, because the head carries ZERO
check-runs — which is exactly the empty-rollup condition BUG-1481 records as reading like a
pass. A conflicted PR with a freshly pushed commit can therefore present as
nothing-failing while nothing has been tested.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR MY OWN PRACTICE, and I would put it in the reviewer discipline rather
than only here: check mergeable_state BEFORE waiting on CI. I polled #2030 for roughly
twelve minutes waiting for a Build that could never start, and the signal that would have
told me instantly was one field away the whole time.

F3 ON #2030 STANDS but its wording is now wrong — it says the cause is undiagnosed. I will
leave the verdict as recorded rather than rewrite it silently, and note here that the cause
is the conflict; if you would rather I re-record it with the mechanism, say so and I will,
the same way you authorized the #2042 rewrite.

THE REVIEW CONSEQUENCE IS UNCHANGED AND SIMPLER THAN BEFORE: there is still no evidence
this rework compiles, and now there cannot be until the conflict is resolved. The rework
needs a rebase before it needs anything else, and F1 and F2 are unaffected by either.
subject: #2030's missing CI diagnosed: the PR is DIRTY, and a commit pushed to a conflicting PR gets no run at all. Merge ref exists but is STALE — my first hypothesis (absent ref) was wrong
